core_obligations: Choose an embedding of the filtered complex into a filtered K-injective complex, as provided by the injectives chapter (proof lines 6843-6846).
Construct the spectral sequence as the one attached to the filtered complex of global sections of the chosen representative, with the filtration induced degreewise (proof lines 6847-6854).

Identify the E_1 page using that cohomology is computed on K-injective representatives, and obtain boundedness and convergence from the filtered complex convergence lemma under the stated vanishing hypotheses (proof lines 6855-6858).
proof_roadmap: Spectral sequence of the filtered complex of global sections (proof lines 6847-6854).
difficulty_reason: For a filtered complex F of O_X-modules on a ringed space, the lemma produces a canonical spectral sequence of bigraded modules over the global sections with E_1 page given by the cohomology of the associated graded pieces, and gives conditions on the filtration under which the spectral sequence is bounded and converges to the cohomology of the complex (statement lines 6821-6838). The proof first embeds F into a filtered K-injective complex, allowed by the existence of such an embedding, and takes the spectral sequence of the filtered complex of global sections of that representative (proof lines 6840-6854). The E_1 page is then identified because cohomology is computed by evaluating on K-injective representatives, and boundedness and convergence under the stated vanishing conditions come from the corresponding statement for filtered complexes (proof lines 6855-6858). The claim is H2: no construction is invented, but the two inputs, the filtered K-injective embedding and the convergence lemma, have to be combined in the right order, and the E_1 identification is the point of the chosen representative.
